context_stem: To make the required showing, we will need to satisfy the following criteria:
excerpt: Audits: Develop plans to (1) audit and assess the design and implementation of the security program and (2) share these findings (and updates on any remediation efforts) with management on an appropriate cadence.
paraphrase: Anthropic must develop plans to audit the security program and share findings and remediation updates with management regularly.

excerpt: We expect this to include independent validation of threat modeling and risk assessment results; a sampling-based audit of the operating effectiveness of the defined controls; periodic, broadly scoped, and independent testing with expert red-teamers who are industry-renowned and have been recognized in competitive challenges.
paraphrase: Anthropic expects audits to include independent validation of threat modeling and risk assessments, sampling-based control audits, and periodic independent testing by renowned expert red-teamers.

context_stem: To make the required showing, we will need to satisfy the following criteria:
excerpt: Third-party environments: Document how all relevant models will meet the criteria above, even if they are deployed in a third-party partner's environment that may have a different set of safeguards.
paraphrase: Anthropic must document how models meet security criteria even when deployed in third-party partner environments with different safeguards.

excerpt: If, after the evaluations above, we determine that we have met the ASL-3 Required Safeguards, then we may proceed with deploying and training models above the Capability Threshold, provided we have also conducted a follow-up capability assessment.
paraphrase: If Anthropic determines it has met the ASL-3 Required Safeguards, it may proceed with deployment and training above the Capability Threshold, contingent on a follow-up capability assessment.

excerpt: The process for determining whether we have met the ASL-3 Required Safeguards is as follows:
paraphrase: The following steps describe the process for determining whether ASL-3 Required Safeguards have been met.

context_stem: The process for determining whether we have met the ASL-3 Required Safeguards is as follows:
excerpt: First, we will compile a Safeguards Report for each Required Safeguard that documents our implementation of the measures above, makes an affirmative case for why we have satisfied them, and advances recommendations on deployment decisions.
paraphrase: Anthropic will first compile a Safeguards Report per Required Safeguard documenting implementation, arguing satisfaction, and recommending deployment decisions.

context_stem: The process for determining whether we have met the ASL-3 Required Safeguards is as follows:
excerpt: The Safeguards Report(s) will be escalated to the CEO and the Responsible Scaling Officer, who will (1) make the ultimate determination as to whether we have satisfied the Required Safeguards and (2) decide any deployment-related issues.
paraphrase: The Safeguards Report will go to the CEO and RSO, who will make the final determination on Required Safeguards satisfaction and decide deployment issues.

context_stem: The process for determining whether we have met the ASL-3 Required Safeguards is as follows:
excerpt: In general, as noted in Sections 7.1.4 and 7.2.2, we will solicit both internal and external expert feedback on the report as well as the CEO and RSO's conclusions to inform future refinements to our methodology.
paraphrase: Anthropic will generally solicit internal and external expert feedback on the report and the CEO/RSO conclusions to refine future methodology.

excerpt: For high-stakes issues, however, the CEO and RSO will likely solicit internal and external feedback on the report prior to making any decisions.
paraphrase: For high-stakes issues, the CEO and RSO will likely seek internal and external feedback before deciding.

context_stem: The process for determining whether we have met the ASL-3 Required Safeguards is as follows:
excerpt: If the CEO and RSO decide to proceed with deployment and training, they will share their decision–as well as the underlying Safeguards Report, internal feedback, and any external feedback–with the Board of Directors and the Long-Term Benefit Trust before moving forward.
paraphrase: If the CEO and RSO decide to proceed, they will share the decision, Safeguards Report, and feedback with the Board and Long-Term Benefit Trust before proceeding.

context_stem: The process for determining whether we have met the ASL-3 Required Safeguards is as follows:
excerpt: After the ASL-3 Required Safeguards are approved, they will be revisited and re-approved at least annually to re-affirm their suitability and sound implementation.
paraphrase: Once approved, ASL-3 Required Safeguards will be reviewed and re-approved at least once a year.

excerpt: If, however, we are unable to make the showing required above, we will restrict model deployment and further scaling.
paraphrase: If Anthropic cannot make the required showing, it will restrict deployment and further scaling of the model.

excerpt: In parallel with upgrading a model to the Required Safeguards, we will (1) update this policy to include any additional Capability Thresholds for which the Required Safeguards would be insufficient; and (2) conduct a follow-up capability assessment to determine that the model's capabilities fall sufficiently far away from those Capability Thresholds, following the procedures outlined in Section 3.
paraphrase: While upgrading a model's safeguards, Anthropic will update the policy for any new insufficient thresholds and conduct a follow-up capability assessment following Section 3 procedures.

excerpt: To summarize the commitments and procedures outlined above, we may deploy or store a model if either of the following criteria are met: (1) the model's capabilities are sufficiently far away from the existing Capability Thresholds, making the current ASL-2 Standard appropriate;
paraphrase: Anthropic may deploy or store a model if its capabilities are sufficiently far from existing Capability Thresholds, keeping ASL-2 appropriate.

excerpt: or (2) the model's capabilities have surpassed the existing Capabilities Threshold, but we have implemented the ASL-3 Required Safeguards and confirmed that the model is sufficiently far away from the next set of Capability Thresholds as to make the model ASL-3 Standard appropriate.
paraphrase: Or the model may be deployed if it has surpassed the existing threshold but ASL-3 Required Safeguards are implemented and confirmed sufficient relative to the next threshold set.
